parsed.title: Bayesian Learning
parsed.description: An intermediate course for university students on the principles and applications of Bayesian Learning. This course covers the foundational Bayes' Theorem, parameter estimation techniques like MLE and MAP, the role of priors, and the implementation of the Naive Bayes classifier.

sections.title: Section 1: Foundations of Bayesian Learning
topics: What is Bayesian Learning?
Why Use Bayesian Methods? Key Motivations
Core Features of the Bayesian Approach
The Bayesian Learning Pipeline: From Prior to Posterior
Distinguishing Learning, Inference, and Decision Making

sections.title: Section 2: The Core Engine: Bayes' Theorem
topics: Understanding Bayes' Theorem and Its Components
Defining Prior, Likelihood, Posterior, and Evidence
Practical Application: Spam Detection Concept
Calculation Walkthrough: A Numerical Example with Spam Filtering

sections.title: Section 3: Estimating Model Parameters
topics: Introduction to Parameter Estimation
Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) Estimation
Connecting MLE, MAP, and Bayes' Rule
Comparing MLE vs. MAP: The Role of Data and Priors

sections.title: Section 4: Parameter Estimation in Practice: A Coin Toss Example
topics: Setting up the Problem: The Bernoulli/Binomial Model
Deriving the MLE for a Coin Bias
Introducing the Beta Prior for MAP Estimation
Deriving the MAP Estimate for a Coin Bias
Review and Comparison: Analyzing MLE vs. MAP Results

sections.title: Section 5: The Role of Prior Knowledge
topics: What is a Prior Distribution?
Types of Priors: Informative, Non-informative, and Conjugate
The Impact of Priors on Learning Outcomes
The Connection Between Priors and Regularization in Machine Learning

sections.title: Section 6: Application: The Naive Bayes Classifier
topics: Introduction to the Naive Bayes Algorithm
The 'Naive' Assumption: Conditional Independence
Strengths and Weaknesses of Naive Bayes
Worked Example: Classifying a Spam Email with Naive Bayes
